# URLCode store

> Operator-installed declarative data store extension for URLCode. Declare
> typed collections in `urlcode.yaml`, mount each with `extension: store`, and
> the extension serves a bounded JSON CRUD API backed by one operator-owned
> SQLite database (`node:sqlite`, Node only). No handler code. Installed with
> `urlcode extensions add store`; not an independent security assessment. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.store: { version: "1", config: { collections: { <name>: { fields, sortable, filterable, readOnly, ... } } } }`
- A mount per collection, e.g. `/api/notes/*: { extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE] }`
- Protect the mount with `auth: true` (the example adds it when auth is installed) unless the
  example's explicit `--ack store:public-write` was given; an unprotected write mount has no rate
  limiting, abuse protection or multi-tenant isolation of its own.
- The store serves JSON only; the frontend is the application's own (`fetch` to the mounts, reading
  `etags` and `may` from a list), as `proofs/private-requests/client` does.
- `urlcode extensions add store` writes an empty `collections` block and no mount; `--example`
  adds the `todos` collection on `/api/todos` (API only); with
  auth installed the mount gets `auth: true` and the collection `ownership: owner` (per-user
  records) and `audit: true`.
- `audit: true` on a collection records every write in the store's own audit log (field names, never
  values): a row of the store database written in the same transaction, kept among the newest `auditRetention`
  events (default 100000). Activation refuses it on a mount no principal-providing policy guards (for example
  `auth: true`). Short-link clicks are never audited. `urlcode-store audit --database <file> [filters]` reads the
  log read-only; `StoreExports.audit` is its query and its tap (`peek`, then `ack`), which a sink extension (it may
  be named `audit`) pulls to forward events, using core's types from `@jimhoyd/urlcode/extensions`.
- `ownership: owner` on a collection scopes every request to the principal a policy such as
  `auth: true` on its mount sets; without it (the default) a collection is shared. An owned
  collection may add `maxRecordsPerOwner: N` (at most `maxRecords`): a principal holding N records
  gets `409 owner_quota_exceeded`; `maxRecords` still caps the whole collection.
- Conditional state changes: `transitions.<name>: {from, set, stamp?, by?, mount?}` on a collection
  serves `POST <mount>/<id>/<name>` (one record, exact `from` values, constant `set` values, `actor`/`now`
  stamps, `If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key`; `409 transition_conflict` otherwise). `by: others` on an owned
  collection lets any principal but the owner act, on its own guarded mount; properties listed in the collection's
  `readOnlyProperties` change only through a transition. `idempotency: {maxKeys}` replays a retried key (same request: first
  status, current record; different request: `422 idempotency_key_reused`). Other multi-record work
  (holds, several collections) uses `StoreExports.transaction(work, {idempotencyKey?, fingerprint?})` in a host
  extension, which with a key keeps `work`'s JSON result (at most 16 KiB) and returns it to a retry without running `work`.
- Transfers between balances: `transfers.<name>: {amount, min?, members?}` on a collection serves
  `POST <mount>/transfers/<name>` with `{from, to, amount}` (two distinct record ids, a positive whole number):
  one transaction subtracts from `from`'s integer `amount` property and adds to `to`'s, so the sum never changes;
  below `min` (default 0) is `409 insufficient_balance` and nothing is written. Owned: the caller debits only its
  own record and may credit anyone's (`to` is answered only when the caller owns it). Integers only (minor units);
  a fraction or `from == to` is `422 invalid_transfer`. `If-Match` (on `from`), `Idempotency-Key` and audit
  (`store.record.transferred` on both records) apply. A members-gated transfer with a negative `min` is an issuer;
  an owned collection refuses a negative `min` without `members`. The amount property is bounded from below only
  (no `maximum`, `multipleOf`, `enum`, `const`), the lowest `min` times `maxRecords` stays within 2^53 - 1, and
  every write reserves the widest balance within `maxRecordBytes`, so any refusal about the credited record is one
  fixed `409 transfer_conflict` that never depends on its balance.
  The amount property must be in `readOnlyProperties` with default 0 and set by no transition; deleting a record
  holding a nonzero amount is `409 balance_not_zero` on every path (HTTP, host transaction `remove`, operator CLI).
- Scheduling: `intervals: {start, end, within?, scope?: collection|owner, when?}` on a collection refuses any
  write whose half-open `[start, end)` overlaps another record's in its scope with `409 interval_conflict`
  (checked in the write's transaction through a partial index; `error.conflict.id` only for a record the
  caller may read, so another owner's booking blocks without being named). Bounds are both numbers or both
  `format: date-time` strings in UTC (`Z`, at most millisecond precision). `length` (`PT1H`, or an integer for
  integer bounds) fixes every slot's length and `step` puts both bounds on a grid from the epoch (`PT1H`: on the
  hour, UTC); a slot breaking either is `422 invalid_record`.
- Edit and delete states: `editable: {status: [draft]}` / `deletable: {status: [draft, rejected]}` (a transition
  `from` shape, each property in `readOnlyProperties`): outside them `PUT`/`PATCH`, an increment or `DELETE` answer
  `409 record_locked` and write nothing (HTTP, `StoreExports`, host transactions), after `If-Match`; creates,
  transitions, transfers and a short link's click count are unaffected. `Allow` on a record and `allow: {<id>: [methods]}` on a list are the hint.
- Unique values: `unique: [handle]` (strings, `maxLength` at most 128, no default, not readOnly, not set by a
  transition) is unique across every owner (`key` stays refused on owned collections); a duplicate create, `PUT` or
  `PATCH` is `409 value_taken`, naming the property only. It tells a caller the value is in use: public handles only.
- Members-only create: `create: {members: <membership collection>}` answers `401` without a principal and `403
  membership_required` to a non-member before the body, the `Idempotency-Key` or any record is read (HTTP,
  `StoreExports` and host transactions alike).
- Stored short links: `extensions.store.config.shortLinks.<name>: {mount, collection, destination, clicks}`
  over a collection with a `key`, a required `format: uri` destination property (HTTP(S) only) and one
  `increments` counter, plus a route `<mount>/*: {extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD]}`; no
  function. See the README's "Short links" example.
- `urlcode-store reassign --database <file> --project <app> --from <id>
  --to <id> [--collection <name>] [--dry-run] [--actor <id>]` moves one principal's records to another in one
  transaction (it may run while the server serves); it refuses as a whole if `--to` would exceed a collection's
  `maxRecordsPerOwner` or would record more audit events than `auditRetention` keeps, records each moved record
  (`store.record.reassigned`) on an `audit: true` collection, and moves `--from`'s membership in every
  `membership: true` collection with the records. `--actor` (default `operator`) is operator-asserted, not
  authenticated. `urlcode-store backup` and `restore` copy the database, audit log included.
- `urlcode-store members add|remove|list --database <file> --project <app> --collection <name> [--principal <id>]`
  maintains a membership collection (no HTTP API exists for it). `audit: true` on it records every added and removed
  member in the same transaction. `readers` is a map of named mounts (`readers: {directory: {...}, audit: {...}}`), each with its own
  `members`, `showOwner` and `properties`. `showOwner: true` shows the owner's principal id as `_owner` on that
  mount only and needs `members`. `properties: [name]` makes a mount a projection (`id` and those properties only, sorted
  and filtered by those only, `ETag` of the projection) and `members` optional: a directory for finding a transfer
  recipient's record id without exposing balances.
- The operator activates it in the site's `host.mjs` with `store()` (or `store({database})`) in
  the `composeHost` list; `urlcode extensions add store` writes that line.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, scaffold, host options, short links, and a generated field reference
  for every configuration key at the end.
- [docs/STORE.md](../../docs/STORE.md): the full HTTP contract, limits and concurrency guarantees.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): trust boundary, the database file, `ETag`/`If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` scoping.

## Do not guess
- No CRUD or persistence code in project `function`/`middleware` routes; declare the
  collection. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no store authority of their own.
- One serving process per database, local disk: a second serving process or a network
  filesystem is refused at activation (an OS lock on `store.sqlite.server-lock`); a retiring
  activation whose collection declaration (or store schema) is older than the newest answers `503
  storage_unavailable` to writes. Each request is one SQLite transaction over one record; last write wins unless a caller sends `If-Match`; a repeated
  `Idempotency-Key` replays the first answer's status with the record as it is now, and the same key on a
  different request is `422`.
- `sortable`/`filterable` field lists are declared per collection; `?sort=`/`?<field>=` queries
  against an undeclared name, or a filter value the field can never hold (outside its `enum`, `minimum`/`maximum`,
  `minLength`/`maxLength` or `format`), are `400`s, not silently ignored.
- The database is operator-owned, outside the project, on local disk, not a network
  filesystem; the store creates its directory `0700` and the file `0600`.
- The `store-schema` artifact is the configuration schema and an example as inert JSON:
  adding it does not register `store` or grant data access.
